1) Deployment custody diagram (PNG) that marks: model storage, KV cache, inference pods, control plane endpoints, and customer VPC boundary.

Quick answers up front:

- Private: control plane operates over a private control-channel; data plane (inference) stays in customer VPC unless the customer enables Redwood-managed telemetry.
- Flow logs: standard offer is 90 days by default; can be extended for enterprise contracts.

Maya — attaching the requested artifacts. Summary below; see attachments for diagrams and a row-level egress inventory.

Attachments: deployment_custody_diagram_v3.png (diagram), egress_matrix_greenline.csv (egress inventory), sig_answers_greenline_v1.docx (SIG snippets)

Executive summary (unique phrasing: custody & traffic contracts)
- Custody boundaries: model binaries and long-term artifacts are stored in Redwood-managed object stores for Hosted/Dedicated builds (customer keys optional). For Private installs, model binaries can be staged to the customer-controlled object store; Redwood does not retain a copy unless customer opts into model update service.
- KV cache and runtime state: ephemeral and kept in the compute enclave (dedicated pod) and backed by local NVMe/instance storage. The KV cache does not persist to central Redwood storage unless configured for snapshotting; snapshots are encrypted and stored with customer or Redwood-managed keys per contract.
- Traffic contracts (how flows are initiated and routed):
  * Dedicated: Inference requests originate from the customer application and reach the Dedicated GPU pool via peering/PrivateLink. Control-plane signals (start/stop/health) originate from Redwood control-plane endpoints to the Dedicated instance over a TLS-secured, mutual-TLS channel that terminates inside the dedicated management VPC. No inference payload is sent to the public internet by default.
  * Private: Deployment control plane endpoints are reachable over a customer-provided private endpoint (VPC endpoint or private link). Data path for inference remains in-customer unless telemetry is enabled.
- Egress and telemetry: by default, telemetry is limited to aggregated metrics (no raw payload). Third-party telemetry vendors are only contacted if the customer enables integrations (e.g., Datadog, Sumo) and provides an outbound endpoint. We do not route raw inference payloads to third parties without explicit config and contract language.
- Flow logs and retention: VPC Flow Logs + application-level audit logs are retained for 90 days by default and archived up to 12 months upon request (enterprise add-on). All logs are encrypted at rest; access is role-scoped and audited.
- Control-plane metadata: control-plane messages contain routing metadata (instance id, region, small operational metadata) but not full inference payloads. When customers enable model updates, digest-level metadata (hashes/checksums) may be sent. We mark PII as never included in control-plane traces; where customers route identifiers, we recommend tokenization at the application boundary.

Open items we noted while packaging the deliverable:
- Confirm desired retention window if Greenline needs >90 days archived.
- Confirm whether Greenline wants telemetry integrations enabled by Redwood as part of the Dedicated project.
